analysis.title: US Economics Analyst: 2027 US Outlook: The End of the Inflation Shocks
key_insights: GS expects 2026 Q4/Q4 real GDP growth of 2.5% despite the Iran war energy shock, in line with its 2026 Outlook forecast and above consensus at the time. Core PCE inflation is expected at 3.2% Q4/Q4 in 2026, worse than the large decline GS and consensus expected at the start of the year.

For 2027, GS forecasts Q4/Q4 GDP growth of 2.4% (consensus 2.2%) and core PCE inflation of 2.4% (in line with consensus). The growth pattern matches 2026: solid consumption and strong business investment offset by drags from housing and trade. GS puts potential growth at 2.3%.

Consumer spending is forecast to grow 2.2% in 2027, driven mainly by real labor income growth as inflation moderates. The 2026 boosts from tax refunds and wealth effects fade, and the saving rate is expected to stay near 5%. Real income growth should be more even across income groups.

AI-related hardware and IPP spending is estimated to exceed $900bn annualized by end-2026 (up $550bn from 2025) and reach $1.4tn by end-2027 (up a further $500bn), roughly 4% of GDP. AI drives half of the 8% business investment growth forecast for 2027.

AI adds only 0.2pp to officially measured 2027 GDP growth because technology goods prices are rising, semiconductor investment is undercounted, and most AI hardware is imported. GS estimates 0.7pp of true GDP growth after adding back undercounted semiconductor investment and chip design exports, or 0.6pp including spillovers.

Midterm election results pose modest risks to AI investment. GS expects newly elected Democratic governors in states with over a third of planned US data center capacity to impose moratoria, but these should be short-lived and affect only projects not yet permitted.

Housing is expected to stay the weakest part of the economy in 2027 on poor affordability. Homebuilding has held up because of the housing shortage, but is likely to become more rate-sensitive as the shortage eases and builder margins normalize. High rates also lock in existing homeowners and dampen turnover.

The labor market is in a slightly softer low-hire, low-fire form of full employment. Layoffs stayed historically low in 2026 despite fears of an AI-driven wave. GS expects this to persist through 2027, with AI displacement pushing unemployment higher in later years.

Wage growth is stabilizing near 3.5% and productivity growth is above 2%, which implies subdued inflationary pressure from labor costs. GS sees little reason for wage acceleration because the labor market is not unusually tight.

The 2026 inflation overshoot came mostly from the Iran war energy shock and AI price pressures. GS says the economy is not overheated at a macro level or an industry level outside AI-related pockets, and inflation expectations do not appear entrenched.

Tariff effects on consumer prices appear to be over and the year-over-year impact is shrinking. GS expects the White House to restore some of the tariffs the Supreme Court ruled unconstitutional, with a very small incremental effect. Tariffs have added 0.9pp to core PCE as of October, with less than 0.1pp still to come.

GS commodity strategists expect Brent near $100/bbl for the next few months, easing to $80/bbl through 2027. In that scenario two-thirds of the commodity passthrough to core PCE is behind us. The war's impact on year-over-year core PCE is 0.5pp now, peaks at 0.6pp, and falls to 0.1pp by end-2027.

AI price pressures currently add 0.45pp to year-over-year core PCE, half from genuine cost pressure and half from mismeasurement in software and accessories. The impact is expected to peak at 0.55pp at end-2026 and fall to about 0.15pp by end-2027, as memory price growth slows with new production capacity.

Core PCE is forecast to fall to 2.4% by Dec 2027 from 3.2% in Dec 2026. The largest declines are expected in tariff-affected goods, airfares (20.3% to -2.4% y/y), consumer electronics, software and accessories, and shelter.

GS expects two more 25bp hikes in December 2026 and March 2027, a total of three, to a peak of 4.25-4.5%. A third hike could come earlier in January, and more than three are possible if the next two inflation reports do not improve. Gradual cuts to 3.25-3.5% are expected to start at the November 2027 meeting. GS says both its baseline and probability-weighted paths are less hawkish than market pricing.

FOMC task forces are expected to produce limited changes. A large balance sheet reduction is unlikely, though a shift toward bills is possible. The Summary of Economic Projections is unlikely to be eliminated entirely.

Main risks are that the inflation shocks last longer or new ones arise, plus downside growth risks from higher oil, prolonged higher rates, and earlier AI job displacement. GS sees most risks as moderate rather than recessionary.

sector_views.rationale: Poor affordability keeps depressing demand, and homebuilding is becoming more sensitive to interest rates as the shortage eases.
AI-related spending drives half of the 8% forecast for 2027 business investment growth, reaching $1.4tn annualized by end-2027.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Growth is above potential despite the energy shock and in line with GS's 2026 Outlook forecast.
A hair above GS's 2.3% estimate of potential, and above consensus on business investment.
Energy shock and AI price pressures leave inflation well above the start-of-year expectation.
Fading tariff, energy and AI price effects drive a substantial decline.
Driven by real labor income as inflation moderates, with fading special factors.
AI adds only 0.2pp to measured GDP growth.
Stable wage growth with productivity above 2% means subdued labor-cost inflation.
Labor market stays stable at near-full employment.
Two more 25bp hikes in Dec 2026 and Mar 2027, less hawkish than market pricing.
Cuts begin at the November 2027 meeting once inflation has fallen meaningfully.
Fading energy pass-through lowers core PCE.
GS table forecast, down from 4.75% at end-2026.

risk_factors: Inflation shocks of the last two years could last longer, or new shocks could arise.
Oil price increases would weigh on real income and consumption.
A longer period of higher interest rates could weigh on growth and reignite fiscal concerns.
Job displacement from AI could come earlier and faster than expected.
AI-enabled cyberattacks are a new risk.
Reescalation of the Iran war or new tariffs.
charts_described: Exhibit 5 shows AI spending in the national accounts rising by $500bn to an annualized pace of $1.4tn by end-2027, slightly less than the $550bn increase in 2026.
Exhibit 17 shows GS fed funds scenario probabilities: three hikes with cuts to 3.25-3.5% (50%), four hikes with a higher terminal rate (35%), recession (15%).
Exhibit 12 notes tariff effects on core PCE of +0.9pp as of October, with less than 0.1pp yet to come, almost all in 2027.
geopolitical: The Iran war energy shock was the main economic surprise of 2026. Its effect on core PCE inflation peaks at 0.6pp and fades to 0.1pp by end-2027.
The Supreme Court ruled some tariffs unconstitutional, and GS expects the White House to replace some of them with a small incremental effect.
GS notes the risk of a reescalation of the war with Iran, but judges it a fairly high bar to match the rate-of-change impact of the past two years.

tension_points.bull_case: Fading tariff, Iran war energy and AI price effects take core PCE to 2.4% by end-2027, allowing Fed cuts from November 2027. The economy is not overheated and expectations are not entrenched.
tension_points.bear_case: The inflation shocks of the last two years could last longer or new shocks could arise, and GS gives 35% odds to four hikes with a higher terminal rate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The next two inflation reports not looking better than GS expects, which could bring a third hike in January or more than three hikes.

tension_points.bull_case: Solid consumption and strong AI-driven business investment keep GDP growth at 2.4%, above consensus at 2.2%.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher oil prices, a longer period of higher rates, or earlier and faster AI job displacement could weigh on growth, though most risks look moderate rather than recessionary.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Oil price increases that weigh on real income growth and consumption, or a sustained tightening in financial conditions.

theme_stances.key_argument: Tariff, energy and AI price effects all fade, so core PCE falls to 2.4% by end-2027 without new shocks.
theme_stances.evidence: inflation will fall substantially by the end of 2027

theme_stances.key_argument: The FOMC stays focused on inflation, hikes in December and March, and cuts from November 2027.
theme_stances.evidence: Both our baseline and probability-weighted Fed forecasts are less hawkish than market pricing.
